chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When a man is the guardian of a man, then for him is his inheritance and upon him is his wergild.

key_terms.وَالَى: to be the guardian or patron of

ai.seo_question: What are the inheritance and financial liabilities of a Saibah's guardian in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the juridical bond of 'Saibah' (unconditional manumission), establishing that the patron (mawla) assumes both the right of inheritance and the liability for blood money (ma'qulah) of the freed slave. In Shia fiqh, this relationship creates a quasi-kinship tie, ensuring the freedman's financial protection and estate succession remain within the patron's lineage, reflecting the social welfare principles of early Islamic society.
